subject: [PATCH v3 0/3] mm: make watermark checks honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain suggested renaming zone_watermark_ok to handle two distinct use cases: checking if there are enough free pages and checking if there are enough free pages that can be allocated, by introducing a new function zone_watermark_ok_for_alloc.
reviews.raw_body:
zone_watermark_ok_mt is a bad name, I am having a hard time figuring out when
to call zone_watermark_ok and when to call zone_watermark_ok_mt. Let us look at
what zone_watermark_ok answers currently, according to the comment above it:

a) "Return true if free base pages are above 'mark'."
b) "For high-order checks it will return true if the order-0 watermark is reached
    and there is at least one free page of a suitable size".

So there are two uses: whether we have enough free pages, then, whether
we have enough free pages *and* we can also allocate.

So let us do something like: we have zone_watermark_ok_for_alloc. It will call
zone_watermark_ok, which will only handle the watermark computation (so this is a
refactor for the code ending at if (!order) line in current zone_watermark_ok).
Then it will also scan the freelists for the correct order, correct migratetype etc.

Then at the callsite we clearly know whether we are just looking for enough free memory,
or whether we are looking for an allocation too.

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a performance issue caused by the high-order watermark check not honouring the ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT flag in memory pressure situations. The check currently counts free pages of every migratetype, leading to incorrect results and stalls in compaction. The patches modify the watermark checks to take into account the request's migratetype and skip free lists that cannot be used. This is achieved by passing the alloc_flags to try_to_free_pages() and modifying the should_reclaim_retry() function. The changes are based on a benchmark that shows significant improvements in performance, with 64K mTHP faults under memory pressure stalling 18 times less often than without the patch series.
